newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog cites Sony ad over portrayal of drugs.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog cites Sony ad over portrayal of drugs.

text.p: Britain's Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) on Wednesday condemned a brochure ad by Sony Music Entertainment for "encouraging irresponsible and anti-social behaviour."

The ad, which was placed in a Club 18-30 holiday brochure, was headlined, "Three essentials for a great holiday. Sex, Drugs and Rock and Roll. We'll provide the rock and roll. You take care of the rest."
The ad featured a picture of some record sleeves, several condoms and a glass of water containing dissolving tablets.
Sony said the ad was "tongue in cheek" and that the tablets pictured were for indigestion and not intended to promote the use of drugs.
But the ASA, the advertising industry's self-regulatory body, said readers would not conclude that tablets were for indigestion and asked Sony not to use the same approach again.
